fieldValues.title: The Pattern Grid has no Process cell, and three dispatch briefs today named one
fieldValues.summary: The dispatch brief for #558 instructed the unit to tag cell:process. There is no Process cell on the Pattern Grid — the twelve cells are fixed, and nothing in the charter admits a thirteenth by convention. The unit corrected to cell:containment plus cell:reference, which is what the RFC's subject matter (a tree of contains edges, referenced by depends-on) actually is.
evidence: srs/docs/charter/decision-compass.md enumerates twelve grid cells; 'Process' is not among them
the-greenman/srs#620 body records the correction: 'the grid has no Process cell; tagged cell:containment + cell:reference'
Three separate dispatch briefs written on 2026-09-06 named a Process cell
fieldValues.body: A brief that names a cell the grid does not have is not a small typo: the Charter Check routes on the cell, and a cell nobody can look up makes the check unfalsifiable. The failure is upstream of the unit — in whatever writes the briefs — so correcting it inside the unit fixes one instance and leaves the source. Recorded as carried context as well, so the next brief-writer reads the rule rather than rediscovering it.
